headline: EU Act stifles. SpinLaunch pivots. True Anomaly cashes.
deck: This week, European regulations face backlash while True Anomaly raises significant capital.

stories.head: EU Space Act could slow competitiveness
stories.body: European industry insiders are expressing concerns that the EU Space Act's bureaucratic nature could hinder competitiveness in the space sector. This is reminiscent of worrying that a traffic jam will ruin your road trip—only the stakes are much higher. With companies like Kongsberg NanoAvionics eyeing sovereign satellite constellations, the timing of these regulations could not be worse.
stories.soWhat: If the EU can't streamline its regulations, it risks losing its competitive edge to more agile players elsewhere.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense pull
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The capital will strengthen its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are becoming increasingly critical to national security. With the DoD's growing interest in these technologies, True Anomaly is positioned to benefit from rising defense budgets.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash flow often trumps tech, this funding signals that True Anomaly is playing the long game—defense contracts are the new gold rush.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team up for SDA
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have announced a partnership to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency constellation. This collaboration highlights a growing trend where defense contractors are realizing that in space, teamwork is essential—unless, of course, you're a satellite with a vendetta. As the SDA focuses on resilient architectures, this bid could reshape the competitive landscape.
stories.soWhat: Expect more partnerships like this as companies seek to pool resources and expertise to meet ambitious government contracts.

watchlist.title: Watch for EU Space Act backlash
watchlist.body: With industry insiders raising alarms, expect a pushback from companies that could lead to regulatory revisions.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: Now that True Anomaly has cash, watch for strategic partnerships that could enhance its market position.

watchlist.title: Anduril's bid outcomes
watchlist.body: The outcome of the Anduril and L3Harris bid could signal shifts in how defense contracts are awarded in the future.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension may indicate a trend where legacy systems continue to dominate despite newer entrants.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
